objectives.summary: The project aims to develop Stylizer VSTi, a virtual music arranger, with a deadline for completion set for July 2014. Key objectives include creating a 32-bit VST plug-in installer for various Windows versions, developing sampled sound font banks, and adding realistic velocity switched samples to the sound banks. The project also plans to involve user contributions for styles and sounds, with a focus on delivering rewards by the project deadline.

Key objectives include creating a VST plug-in for various Windows versions, developing sound banks, and enabling user contributions to the project.

The project aims to add realistic velocity switched samples to the provided sound banks for the first two style's generic banks.

innovation.summary: The project demonstrates innovation through the development of the Stylizer software, which features advanced sound design capabilities, including the ability to play sounds across 16 channels and sync to host tempo. It incorporates a range of functionalities such as MIDI automation, realistic sampled sound fonts, and user-friendly features like style recall buttons and a master panning knob.
key_points: Stylizer can design sounds and play them along 16 channels simultaneously depending on the computer's CPU and memory.
The software features a full MIDI automated interface and includes realistic sampled sound fonts banks.
Users can assign scales to styles and transpose the whole style to a key, enhancing user control over sound design.
The project will include features such as solo and mute buttons on the interface and a master delay tempo sync function.
Stylizer enables part looping and auto fill-in capability, providing dynamic sound creation options.
The project will use, edit, and re-sample public domain general midi banks to add to their own sampled library called 'mostly solo instruments'.
